Visiting the Auditor’s Office at City Hall

We're open Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. We accept in-person visits Tuesday to Thursday at City Hall in room 130. For more information about how to connect with us either in person or remotely, please see our contact information on our homepage or visit our contact information webpage.

What's on the Portland ballot | November 3, 2026

Label: Information
View full size image of A hand holding a pen. hovering over an RCV ballot.
On this page, you will find information about what will be included on the November 3, 2026 General Election ballot for Portlanders.

On this page

City of Portland candidates

City offices on the ballot

City of Portland will be electing the following positions in November using ranked choice voting: 

  • One City Auditor (four-year term)
  • Three City Councilors for District 3 (four-year terms)
  • Three City Councilors for District 4 (four-year terms)

Find your City Council District by address

City of Portland measures

The following measure was proposed by initiative petition for the November 3, 2026, General Election ballot. Visit the Portland measures webpage to view the ballot title, text of the legislation, and other information about this measure. 

Measure 26-267

Amends Charter: Portland residents decide 2% of city's annual discretionary budget.

Question: Should Portland create participatory budgeting program for residents to make binding decisions to spend 2% of city's discretionary budget?

Other items on your ballot

City of Portland voters will receive their November 2026 General Election ballots from their voting county (Multnomah, Clackamas, or Washington County). To find out more about what specific contests, candidates, and measures are on your ballot, contact your county elections office:

Voting frequently asked questions

When will I receive my ballot? 

Ballots will be mailed out to County residents beginning October 14. If you have not received your ballot by October 22, contact your local county elections office: 

County elections officePhoneEmail
Multnomah County Elections503-988-8683elections@multco.us
Clackamas County Elections503-655-8510elections@clackamas.us
Washington County Elections503-846-5800Elections@washingtoncountyor.gov

Where can I go to vote or return my ballot? 

Official drop box sites

Special drop boxes just for ballots are located around the state and are available 24 hours a day to collect ballots. Voters can deposit their ballots until 8:00 PM on Election Day. Voters who are already in line at 8:00 PM are allowed to drop off their ballot.

Multnomah County drop boxes

Clackamas County drop boxes

Washington County drop boxes

State of Oregon ballot drop box locator map

Vote by mail 

Oregonians can vote by taking their ballot to the post office or placing in a local mailbox. The Oregon Secretary of State recommends mailing your ballot by October 27 to ensure your vote is received in time to be counted.  

Use this map to find a Portland mailbox near you

Vote in person

Voting ends at 8:00 PM on Election Day. Voters who are already in line at 8:00 PM will still be allowed to vote.

Multnomah County (two locations)

  • Multnomah County Elections Office

    Portland, OR 97214
  • Gresham Voting Center Express

    Gresham, OR 97030

How can I get information on the status of my ballot? 

Sign up for Track Your Ballot. You will receive an alert when your ballot is mailed out to you. After you vote and return your ballot, Track Your Ballot will notify you when your ballot has been received by the elections office, and again when it has been accepted for counting.

Multnomah County: Track your ballot

Clackamas County: Track your ballot

Washington County: Track your ballot

Or sign up through the Oregon Secretary of State's Office: Track your ballot

What if I need help with my ballot (for example: not received, lost, filled out incorrectly, disability accommodations needed, absentee ballot needed)?

Contact your local county elections office for help with any issues with your ballot:
